newsitem.title: FRANCE: Veteran French journalist Jacques Decornoy dies.
newsitem.headline: Veteran French journalist Jacques Decornoy dies.

text.p: Veteran French journalist Jacques Decornoy, best known for his reporting from Vietnam at the height of American involvement in Southeast Asia, died of cancer in Paris on Monday, aged 59, the daily Le Monde said on Tuesday.

Decornoy's reports from the field in both South and North Vietnam in the late-1960s, at a time when Hanoi was not easily accessible to Western journalists, drew wide attention in France and elsewhere.
He was appointed head of the newspaper's Asian coverage in 1972 and became foreign editor in 1977.
An unsuccessful candidate to be Le Monde's editor-in-chief in 1979, he left the newspaper in 1983 to join TF1 television where he coordinated news magazine programmes.
He left TF1 in 1987, returning to the Le Monde stable, where he worked at its sister publication, the monthly Le Monde Diplomatique.
